author: bd-spin/bd-spin-20260512T162003Z-2147161
text:
Pre-claim architectural question surfaced by JMAP-g7wu.2.4.12 close (revert completed 2026-05-12).

The 2026-05-12 re-scoped acceptance requires (criteria 1-3):
  1. Permission gating via Self::principal_id(caller)
  2. Role-hierarchy enforcement (caller's highest role position vs target role)
  3. Last-admin-protection knob (config-gated permission-graph check)

Criterion 7 says: when principal_id returns None, allow all ops without identity-dependent checks.

MemoryBackend has type CallerCtx = (); JmapBackend::principal_id is a STATIC method taking &CallerCtx, default-impl returns None. With CallerCtx = (), MemoryBackend's principal_id can ONLY return None. This means criteria 1-3 implementation will be compile-but-never-exercised dead code under MemoryBackend's existing tests — a workspace test-integrity violation (workspace AGENTS.md: "Never write a test that uses the code under test as its own oracle"; the implementation-without-test-coverage shape is the same failure mode).

How should we make the identity-gated enforcement paths testable? Four options:

OPTION A — Change MemoryBackend's CallerCtx from () to Option<Id>. Override principal_id to return caller.as_ref(). Existing tests update from &() to &None. Largest churn (~1000+ LOC across tests/integration.rs and tests/common/), but cleanest architecturally. Touches every chat-server test site.

OPTION B — Keep CallerCtx = (). Add force_principal_id_for_test: Option<Id> to Inner with a #[doc(hidden)] setter. apply_space_patch calls a helper that resolves caller_id via B::principal_id(caller).cloned().or_else(|| inner.force_principal_id_for_test.clone()). Breaks the principal_id abstraction (only this call site reads the override), but minimal change footprint and zero existing-test churn.

OPTION C — Build a separate test-only backend in tests/common/ with type CallerCtx = Id and principal_id returning Some(caller). Test the enforcement paths against THAT backend. MemoryBackend stays single-user-mode-only and tests for it cover only the None branch. Matches the existing FaultyBackend/MockBackend precedent (per integration.rs:1230, 4623). The test backend would re-export or wrap MemoryBackend's logic to avoid duplicating apply_space_patch.

OPTION D — Implement enforcement, skip testing. Violates workspace test-integrity rule. Rejected.

Recommendation: OPTION C. It keeps MemoryBackend's single-user-mode posture clean (matches workspace AGENTS.md "Caller identity (foundation seam)" note that test fixtures return None), uses a focused ~150-200 LOC test backend dedicated to identity-gated coverage, and matches the existing precedent of test-only backends for negative paths. The trade-off is slightly more test infrastructure vs Option B's API-shape compromise.

The bead's size estimate (~600-800 LOC + tests) does not include this test-infrastructure decision, so confirming the approach before claiming would let the implementer scope tests correctly.

Adjacent question — protect_last_admin knob shape: bead says "expose a MemoryBackend config knob (e.g. protect_last_admin: bool, default false)". Should this knob also be exposed on the ChatBackend trait (with a default-true impl) so production backends can opt in via override, or strictly MemoryBackend-only? The set_limits_for_test precedent (workspace AGENTS.md "Backend caps and limits") is a trait-level method with a grouped struct; a single bool knob doesn't naturally fit ChatLimits. Recommendation: file a dedicated trait method ChatBackend::protect_last_admin(&self, caller, account_id) -> bool with default true, and a parallel set_protect_last_admin_for_test setter on MemoryBackend Inner — same shape pattern as limits() but with a bool return rather than a struct. The bead text leaves "MemoryBackend config knob" intentionally narrow; trait-vs-backend scope confirmation would let the implementer write the right shape on the first pass.

Both decisions feed into how the bead should be scoped — Option C/B/A is gating, and the protect_last_admin shape affects ~50 LOC of API surface.
